title: Chicago Construction Codes (DOB code navigation page)
publisher: City of Chicago Department of Buildings
keyFacts: The Chicago Electrical Code is Title 14E of the Municipal Code and incorporates provisions of the 2017 National Electrical Code (NFPA 70) by reference; the NEC text is not reprinted in the ordinance (Electrical section).

A free read-only compiled Chicago Electrical Code (NEC + Chicago amendments) is hosted by NFPA at link.nfpa.org/free-access/publications/70/2017Chicago; a compiled copy can be purchased from NFPA (Electrical section).
Full text of Title 14E (read only) and 'amendments only' are published by American Legal Publishing (Chicago Electrical Code (14E) row).
Chicago Construction Codes cover building, electrical, fire, plumbing, mechanical etc. in Titles 14A (administration), 14B, 14C, 14E, 14F, 14G, 14M, 14N, 14P, 14R, 14X (code list).
notes: Page body text still describes Phase 2 as 'will be phased in between June 2019 and August 2020' - parts of the page are stale; the Phase 3 (2026) alerts in the sidebar are current. No electrical-code edition change found as of 2026-11-14.

title: Modernizing Chicago's Construction Codes (DOB code modernization history)
publisher: City of Chicago Department of Buildings
keyFacts: Phase 1: the new Chicago Electrical Code (based on the 2017 NEC) was adopted in September 2017 and became mandatory March 1, 2018 (Phase 1 section).

Electrical code ordinances listed: Electrical Code Adoption (Sept 6, 2017), Electrical Code Technical Corrections (Nov 8, 2017), Technical Corrections to Electrical and Conveyance Device Codes (Jan 23, 2019) (Phase 1 section).
In 2015 the Electrical Commission was reinstated to develop the update (Phase 1 section).

Phase 3 Construction Code Modernization Ordinance adopted June 17, 2026; transition memo dated October 6, 2026 (2026 section). Phase 3 is described as fire code, mechanical, plumbing/energy and other provisions - not the electrical code (Phase 3 heading).
notes: The linked Legistar copy of the 2017 adoption ordinance returned 'Gone'; chicago.gov /content/dam PDFs (transition memo, Phase 3 ordinance SO2026-0024930, 2017 presentation) returned HTTP 403 to automated download and were not saved.

title: Press release: Chicago One of First Major Cities to Align with the 2017 National Electrical Code
publisher: City of Chicago Department of Buildings
keyFacts: City Council adopted the Chicago Electrical Code update aligned with the 2017 NEC on September 6, 2017 (press release body).
Approximately half of the 156 NEC articles were adopted with no local amendments; many others with only minor amendments (press release body).
Chicago retained strict requirements for the use of metal conduit and longstanding requirements on emergency lighting and emergency generators (press release body).
The update expanded use of flexible metal conduit for residential and non-residential rehabilitation (press release body).
New lighting load calculation methods allow up to an 83% reduction in lighting design loads (press release body).
The Electrical Commission includes Buildings, Fire Department, journeyman electrician, electrical contractor and electric utility representatives (press release body).
notes: Summary-level only; the precise amended text (e.g., 14E-3-334 NM cable limits) is in Title 14E / the NFPA compiled code, which could not be retrieved (American Legal returned 403).

title: Press release: City Council passes ordinance to update sections of building code (Electrical & Conveyance technical corrections)
publisher: City of Chicago Department of Buildings
keyFacts: Ordinance passed January 23, 2019 updates and cleans up the Electrical Code (14E) and Conveyance Devices Code (14C) (body).
The updates took effect February 1, 2019 (body).
Beginning July 1, 2019, Chicago licensed plumbers need 4 hours CE for renewal (body) - plumbing only; no electrician CE stated.

title: Alert: Implementation of Phase 3 Construction Codes Modernization Ordinance (Oct 6, 2026)
publisher: City of Chicago Department of Buildings
keyFacts: As of October 1, 2026 applicants may elect the 2026 Chicago Fuel Gas, Mechanical and Energy Transformation Codes plus amendments to the 2019 Building Code, Rehabilitation Code and Administrative Provisions (alert body).
The new provisions are mandatory for permit applications started on or after December 1, 2026 (alert body).
The alert does not list the Chicago Electrical Code (14E) among the updated codes (alert body).
notes: Optional from 2026-10-01, mandatory 2026-12-01. Commissioner's transition memo (CodeMemo2026-001.pdf) returned 403 - not read; whether Phase 3 contains incidental 14E amendments is unverified.

title: Press release: Mayor and DOB celebrate passage of Phase 3 of the Construction Codes Modernization (June 17, 2026)
publisher: City of Chicago Mayor's Press Office
keyFacts: Phase 3 updates five code areas: mechanical, fuel gas, fire prevention, energy and residential construction (body).
Phase 3 was introduced to City Council April 15, 2026; complete ordinance is on the City Clerk's website (body).
notes: Used to confirm the electrical code is not among the Phase 3 code areas.

title: Building permit terms and conditions: Electrical Work (Express Permit Program)
publisher: City of Chicago Department of Buildings
keyFacts: Electrical work must comply with the edition of the Chicago Electrical Code in effect when the permit application was submitted (General).
Electrical work must be performed by the Chicago-licensed electrical contractor listed on the permit application (General).

Existing deficiencies in the building electrical system, including grounding and bonding, must be corrected as part of any permitted electrical work and identified in the application; the contractor must investigate existing conditions first (Existing electrical deficiencies).
A 'repair or alter devices on existing circuits' permit may not add circuits, replace a panel, replace/upgrade a service or add outdoor site lighting (Permit to Repair or Alter...).
Express 'new service or service disconnecting means' permits cannot cover services or disconnects rated 1,200 A or more, nor generators (Permit for New Electrical Service...).
New fixtures/equipment must meet the Chicago Energy Transformation Code (Energy efficiency).

title: Express Permit Program instructions: Electrical Work
publisher: City of Chicago Department of Buildings
keyFacts: Express 'Electrical Work' covers stand-alone electrical work not associated with another building permit; signs, wireless equipment, fire alarm, solar PV, HVAC and multiple contractors on one permit are excluded (intro).

Six electrical subtypes: repair/alter devices on existing circuits; add circuits to existing panel; new service/disconnect (<1,200 A); generator; low voltage/communication; new outdoor site lighting (subtype list).

Electrical drawings with single-line diagram and load calcs are required for e.g. generators, new services 400 A or larger or 277 V+, EVSE serving 4+ spaces, and service/panel work in residential buildings 3+ stories or non-residential 2+ stories (Required documents).

A licensed electrical contractor (general) is required for most electrical work; a low-voltage contractor may do low-voltage/communication only; an Illinois-licensed private alarm contractor may do private alarm work (Required contractor).
If the scope includes EV supply equipment, the installer's Illinois Commerce Commission EV Charging Station Installer Certification number must be provided (Required contractor).
Related code sections cited: 14A-12-1204.2 (fees), 14R-4-406 (Repairs - Electrical), Chapter 14X-7 (Electrical requirements for existing buildings) (References).

title: Express Permit Program instructions: Electrical Maintenance (Monthly)
publisher: City of Chicago Department of Buildings
keyFacts: A monthly electrical maintenance permit lets a single licensed electrical contractor do eligible maintenance at a property over 30 days while keeping a detailed log (overview).
It can also cover temporary wiring and portable outdoor generators for indoor/outdoor special events and trade shows (overview).
Not allowed under it: replacing/upgrading a service, signs, wireless equipment, fire alarm work, permanent exit signs, space heating, water heating, solar PV (ineligible list).

title: What types of work do not require a building permit? Electrical Work
publisher: City of Chicago Department of Buildings
keyFacts: No permit is needed for minor work such as replacing a lamp or plugging cord-and-plug equipment into a permanently installed receptacle (list item 1).

No permit for FCC-regulated radio/TV transmission equipment itself (power supply wiring, towers and antennas still need a permit), for temporary test/service systems, or for low-voltage fixtures such as cameras, phones, speakers, doorbells or thermostats (list).

Low-voltage wiring generally needs a permit, except installing/altering low-voltage or communication wiring in a residential building up to 4 stories (and its accessory buildings) is exempt (residential exception).
Exceptions may not apply to Chicago Landmarks; exempt work must still comply with the Chicago Construction Codes (Section 14A-4-402) (closing paragraphs).
notes: Note: device/receptacle replacement is not on Chicago's exemption list (contrast with Philadelphia).

title: Electrical Inspections (DOB Electrical Inspection Bureau)
publisher: City of Chicago Department of Buildings
keyFacts: The Electrical Bureau inspects electrical installations, responds to complaints, and does annual inspections of nursing homes, day care centers, electrical signs and public places of assembly; it also inspects fire alarms and life-safety emergency systems (body).
Owners cannot do their own electrical work in Chicago - only electrical contractors licensed by the City of Chicago may perform electrical installations (FAQ).
Electrical permit applications must list the licensed contractor(s) performing the work (Additional Information).

title: Supervising Electrician License
publisher: City of Chicago Department of Buildings
keyFacts: An electrical contractor must be owned by or employ at least one licensed supervising electrician, who performs or supervises all its electrical work; a supervising electrician may be primary for only one contractor (FAQ: When is a license required).
Two exam types: general and low voltage (other specializations offered before 2018) (FAQ: types).
Eligibility: at least 21 years old and at least 2 years' experience under a supervising electrician or equivalent, verified by supervisor letters; written exam required (FAQ: requirements).
Applications and exams are handled by Continental Testing Services; failed applicants wait at least 6 months to reapply (FAQ: apply).
2026 fees: exam $150 per exam, initial license $150, renewal $150/year; license valid one year; cannot renew if expired 3+ years (FAQ: cost/validity).
Governing ordinance: Municipal Code of Chicago Chapter 4-292 (Ordinances and Rules).
notes: No reciprocity path for out-of-state licenses is described on the page - an out-of-state electrician appears to need the Chicago exam (inference; not stated).

title: Electrical Contractor License
publisher: City of Chicago Department of Buildings
keyFacts: A Chicago electrical contractor license is required to install, alter or maintain any wiring/equipment regulated by the Chicago Electrical Code, whether or not a permit is required; exceptions only for ICC-regulated public utilities and state-licensed private alarm contractors (FAQ: when required).
Work may be done only by the licensed business and its W-2-type employees under a licensed supervising electrician; independent contractors are not covered (FAQ: who can perform).

'Class 1' work (buildings over 55 ft, or Group A assembly with occupant load 300+, before a certificate of occupancy) requires every worker to be a supervising electrician, a graduate of a US DOL-recognized 8,000-hour apprenticeship, or currently enrolled in one; records kept 2 years (FAQ: employee requirements).
Two license types: general and low voltage (Class 1/2/3 remote-control, signaling, power-limited and communications circuits only) (FAQ: types).

Applications processed by Continental Testing Services; 2026 fees $150 initial / $150 renewal; valid one year; auto-inactivated if no valid supervising electrician is associated (FAQ: apply/cost/validity).

title: 65 ILCS 5/11-33-1 (Illinois Municipal Code) - municipal registration of electrical contractors
publisher: Illinois General Assembly
keyFacts: Municipalities 'may require' registration of electrical contractors and may charge an annual $25 registration fee (Sec. 11-33-1, para. 1).
A contractor registered in one municipality shall not be required by another municipality to register or pay a fee (Sec. 11-33-1, para. 1).
'Electrical contractor' excludes radio receiving equipment, public-utility equipment under ICC jurisdiction, and the contractor's employees (Sec. 11-33-1, para. 2).
Source note: Laws 1961, p. 576 (statute footer).
notes: This is local-option authority; the statute itself creates no state electrician license. Whether the cross-municipality rule binds home-rule Chicago (which runs its own exam-based licensing under MCC 4-290/4-292) is NOT verified. No IDFPR electrician license was found; 'Illinois has no statewide electrical license' is consistent with this but no single official statement saying so was retrieved.

title: 83 Ill. Adm. Code 469.10 Definitions (ICC certification for EV charging station installation)
publisher: Illinois Joint Committee on Administrative Rules / Illinois Commerce Commission
keyFacts: 'Qualified person' for EV charger work: completed at least 5 EV charging station installations, or a DOL-registered journeyman electrician apprenticeship, or a UL EV charging station installation certification program (469.10 'Qualified person').
'Self-installer' = individual installing a charger for personal use on own premises without help (469.10).
'Install' means connecting, per applicable building and electrical codes, the conductors and equipment delivering energy from premises wiring to the EV charging station (469.10).
notes: Local URL suffix 100R corresponds to Section 469.10.

title: 83 Ill. Adm. Code 469.20 Applicability (EV charging station installer certification)
publisher: Illinois Joint Committee on Administrative Rules / Illinois Commerce Commission
keyFacts: After January 1, 2014, except self-installers, all persons/entities installing, maintaining or repairing EV charging stations in Illinois must be certified by the Illinois Commerce Commission beforehand (469.20).
notes: Chicago express permits require the ICC EV installer certification number when EVSE is in scope.

title: ComEd Service and Meter Requirements (2025 Edition)
publisher: Commonwealth Edison Company (ComEd)
keyFacts: Title page '2025 Edition'; change log entries dated 2025-03-28, 2025-06-27 and 2025-09-26 (pp.1-2).

Specifications conflicting with this book ceased to be effective January 1, 2017; work to the older 'Silver Book' (Information and Requirements for the Supply of Electric Service) is not accepted for new/revised service (p.4).

Customer must obtain permits and inspections; ComEd is usually prohibited by municipal authorities from connecting service to an installation that has not passed inspection (p.4 'Compliance to Codes').
ComEd asks for at least two weeks' notice for overhead service drops and up to twelve weeks for larger installations (p.4).

Self-contained metering required at 480 V or less for disconnects up to 200 A three-phase, 350 A single-phase non-residential, 400 A single-phase residential; meter equipment must be CECHA-approved ringless with bypass (C9111 §3.1-3.2, p.70).

Meter devices on or within 6 ft of the building are bonded to the building grounding system per the local electrical code - no separate ground rod; pole/pedestal meters >6 ft away need a separate rod (p.64).
Dig-safe: JULIE 8-1-1 outside Chicago; DIGGER (312) 744-7000 inside Chicago (p.6 contacts).
